messages:
acmeops: Hey team — our private inference fleet in VPC (subnet 10.3.4.0/24) started failing streaming responses yesterday evening. Clients report mid-stream disconnects and our proxy logs show `tls: unexpected message` and `SSL: wrong version number`. Any quick checks?

priya-support: Sorry about that. Are you routing egress through a corporate TLS-inspecting proxy or WAF? Also paste the SG and NACL rules for the affected subnets.

acmeops: Yes, outbound goes through a perimeter WAF that does TLS inspection + an edge firewall with a strict allowlist. NACLs look like this (redacted):
- 100 ALLOW TCP 443 0.0.0.0/0 (egress)
- 110 DENY ALL ANY 0.0.0.0/0 (egress default)
- 100 ALLOW TCP 443 0.0.0.0/0 (ingress)
- 120 DENY ALL ANY 0.0.0.0/0 (ingress default)

samir-sre: That NACL is suspicious for client TLS flows. Remember NACLs are stateless — you must allow ephemeral ports (1024-65535) in both directions so server replies to client source ports aren't dropped. Also, if the WAF terminates and re-initiates TLS, it must present certs trusted by the client or the client will abort.

lina-engineering: Can you capture a short tcpdump showing the TLS handshake (ClientHello) and what follows? If you see an immediate RST after ClientHello that suggests either the WAF rejected the flow or the return path is getting dropped.

acmeops: Pulled a tiny pcap, redacted IPs:
```
12:24:11.001 IP 10.3.4.21.52234 > 52.19.44.77.443: Flags [S], seq 0
12:24:11.002 IP 52.19.44.77.443 > 10.3.4.21.52234: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1
12:24:11.003 IP 10.3.4.21.52234 > 52.19.44.77.443: Flags [.], ack 1
12:24:11.100 IP 10.3.4.21.52234 > 52.19.44.77.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 1  <-- ClientHello
12:24:11.101 IP 52.19.44.77.443 > 10.3.4.21.52234: Flags [R], seq 0, ack 0  <-- RST right after ClientHello
```

priya-support: That RST is the smoking gun. Two likely culprits: 1) WAF is terminating or inspecting and actively sending a TLS alert/RST for that flow; 2) NACL/firewall asymmetry dropping the translated return and the remote closing. Does your WAF do SNI rewrite or cert replacement?

acmeops: WAF does TLS inspection and replaces certs with its own signed by our corporate CA (clients trust that CA). It can also do SNI-based passthrough if configured.

samir-sre: Try a direct curl from an instance in the subnet with verbose TLS to see where the handshake fails: 
```
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.com:443:52.19.44.77 https://api.redwood.com/v1/health
```
Look for `CLIENT HELLO` then `SERVER HELLO`. If the server hello never arrives and you get a RST/ALERT, that points to WAF or NACL.

acmeops: Ran curl -v, got: 
```
* Connected to api.redwood.com (52.19.44.77) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), CLIENT HELLO
* TLSv1.3 (IN), ALERT: fatal (unknown)
* ERROR: TLS: wrong version number
```

lina-engineering: `ALERT: fatal` could be from your WAF (inspecting device) or from the remote if it sees a malformed/replayed ClientHello. Since bypassing inspection may not be trivial, try: 1) temporarily add a WAF passthrough rule for `api.redwood.com`, or 2) allow ephemeral port ranges in the NACL for both ingress and egress (1024-65535).

priya-support: Also check your border firewall allowlist: make sure outbound TCP 443 to the Redwood egress IP ranges is allowed, and that return ephemeral ports are permitted. If you use a NAT gateway vs no-NAT setup, connection tracking behavior changes — NAT is usually simpler for client-originated TLS.

acmeops: I updated the NACL to explicitly allow 1024-65535 on both ingress and egress and requested a WAF passthrough for the `api.redwood.com` host. After that, streaming sessions stayed up and we stopped seeing TLS errors.

samir-sre: Nice. That confirms it was the combination of stateless NACL + TLS-inspecting WAF causing asymmetric/terminated flows. For a long-term fix: either keep SNI passthrough for Redwood endpoints, ensure the WAF presents certs trusted by your clients and preserves TLS extensions, or route outbound through a NAT gateway so your edge firewall/NACLs don't need per-ephemeral rules.

priya-support: If you see intermittent reoccurrence, capture full pcap + WAF logs and we can escalate to an engineer-led debug. Glad it's stable now :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Incident linked: INC-2025-0817 — workspace: support — priority: P2 — assignee: priya-support

acmeops: Thanks all, will monitor and re-open if we spot anything else.
